children: China's top copper smelters agreed on Tuesday not to set fourth-quarter guidance for copper concentrate processing fees, sources said, as they discuss production cuts amid acute feedstocks shortage. This is the seventh consecutive quarter where they  have not provided the indicator.

The decision was made at a quarterly meeting of the China Smelters Purchase Team (CSPT), composed of dozens of major smelters in the world's top producer, according to two sources with knowledge of the matter.
The quarterly guidance used to serve as a benchmark for spot copper concentrate deals in China.
CSPT also called on smelters to trim output to counter falling processing fees, said one of the sources.

The treatment and refining charges (TC/RC), paid by miners to smelters for converting copper concentrate into refined metal, have stayed negative for 21 months, signaling an acute tightness of concentrate supply.
Spot processing fees were assessed at minus $226.2 a metric ton on September 18, versus minus $215.9 a week earlier and minus $41.6 a year before, data from information provider Argus showed.

"TC/RCs continue to slide with no clear inflection point in sight, while weakening sulfuric acid prices have substantially eroded smelters' profitability," analysts at broker Zijin Tianfeng Futures said in a note.
